plan.about: The audit plan the F1 Finance Audit Machine follows for the year-end audit of the invented HANGS Construction Services LLC, fiscal year 2026. The runner reads its thresholds, sample and filters from here; the Audit Files system shows it. Every name and figure is invented.
plan.reader: The shareholders, the bonding company and Cinderbrook Bank read the year-end statements; the board of directors receives the findings.

materiality.why: The same materiality serves every FY2026 audit area. The engagement partner sets the final amounts.

populations.name: Subcontractor pay applications
populations.rule: Vendor invoices to account 5100 of $10,000 or more

populations.name: Other vendor invoices
populations.rule: Vendor invoices to the other cost and expense accounts of $10,000 or more, except use tax and the two key items

sample.why: Each population is numbered by ledger entry and drawn without repeats by a fixed pseudo-random generator started from the seed, so anyone can draw the sample again. The key items are tested whatever the draw: the year's largest legal invoice and a June 30 payable.

filters.name: Manual, over the threshold, the Controller's, no independent approval
filters.rule: A manual entry whose debits exceed the policy's $25,000 review threshold, prepared by the Controller, with no approver or approved by herself

filters.name: Round amounts
filters.rule: A manual entry of $10,000 or more whose debits are a whole multiple of $1,000

filters.name: Weekends and after hours
filters.rule: Posted by a person on a Saturday or Sunday, or before 6:00 AM or after 8:00 PM

filters.name: Revenue, cash or WIP late in the year, or after the close
filters.rule: A manual entry dated June 15 to 30, 2026 with a line to revenue, cash or the over and under billings, or any FY2026 entry posted after the June subledgers closed

filters.name: Unusual account pairs
filters.rule: A two-account entry whose debit and credit accounts appear together in no other entry of the year

filters.name: Seldom-used accounts
filters.rule: An entry with a line to an account used by four or fewer entries in the year

filters.name: Reversed right after year end
filters.rule: An FY2026 entry reversed by an entry dated July 1 to 15, 2026

search.why: The search for unrecorded bills reads every payment after June 30 of $10,000 or more and every legal, professional and utility bill, the liabilities area's scope.

assertions.assertion: The books are complete and agree
assertions.how: The trial balance recomputed from the June 30, 2025 balances and every FY2026 ledger line; the statements agreed to the trial balance
A seeded sample of vendor invoices vouched to the invoices; every invoice on file traced back to the books
Every customer receipt in the ledger matched to the bank's own deposit report
Every payment after June 30 in scope set against the June 30 payables and the work it paid for
Every journal entry run through the seven filters, and every high-risk entry followed up with its support
Every dividend agreed to the board's declaration and the bank's payment confirmation; equity rolled forward
The bank's own confirmation and statement agreed to the ledger through the reconciling items

procedures.what: Recompute the trial balance from every ledger line, agree it to the statements and propose materiality from revenue, as the plan sets it.
Draw a seeded sample of vendor invoices and vouch it, trace every vendor invoice on file back to the books, and match every customer receipt to the bank's deposit report.
Set the payments after June 30 against the June 30 payables, check the cutoff and last year's payables, and scan the expenses for anything to capitalize.
Prove the population, run the seven filters, roll the warranty reserve forward, agree the dividends to the board and follow up every high-risk entry.
Tie cash and the loans to the bank's own letter and statement, and compare the year with last year and each month with the rest.
Add up every area's proposed adjustments against materiality and write the workpapers and the draft findings memo. The CPA concludes.

otherAreas.about: The other FY2026 areas’ proposed adjustments, each as its own workpapers and draft memo give it: carried into the summary by id and amount. All reduce FY2026 income.

known.what: Pier 9 CO-07 revenue the signed change order does not support
Kestrel Point credit agreed June 18, recorded in July
Employer taxes on the accrued wages
Payroll account bank charges never recorded
SALE-01, CAP-01, DEP-01 and LEASE-01, net

cross.what: Pier 9 revenue at cost-to-cost once UL-01 is recorded

covenant.what: June 30, 2026 tangible net worth and the loan agreement's minimum (Section 7.6)

cash.about: The cash audit’s June 30 reconciliation: the checks written before June still outstanding, and the stale one.
